RAJYA  SABHA

List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the October 17, 2008/Asvina 25, 1930 (Saka)

(Ministries; Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions  20
1
Dengue deaths
*1.  SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN TIWARI:
SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that fifteen States
in the country are in the grip of dengue;
(b) if so, the number of persons who
died of dengue and whether Government is
planning to formulate a country-wide plan
to control this disease; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Investment plans of steel companies
*2. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that of late major
steel companies in the country have
announced investment plans;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the tangible progress made therein;
and
(d) the role of Government in
supporting these steel companies in their
investment plans?
Promoting eye donations
*3. SHRIMATI  SUPRIYA SULE: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether eye donations in the
country have increased this year but are
still far from the target of two lakh corneas;
(b) whether to encourage eye donations,
his Ministry has urged Government to
increase one time financial assistance given
to the 500 odd eye banks in the country;
(c) whether during the current year, eye
collection is 32,000 but the need is to collect
at least one lakh eyes every year;
(d) whether his Ministry has also laid
emphasis on Cornea Retrieval Programme;
and
(e) to what extent more aid to eye banks
has helped to boost eye donations?
Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

2
Infant deaths due to clinical trials at
AIIMS
*4. SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as many as
49 babies had died at the AIIMS while being
subjected to clinical trials for testing new
drugs and therapies;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government has set up a
special committee to probe reports of the
deaths of children during clinical trials at
the hospital and asked them to submit
report within a week;
(d) if so, the details of the report
submitted by the committee;
(e) whether Government proposes to
review the policy of clinical trials; and
(f) if so, the details thereof?
Bogibeel Rail-cum-Road Bridge
*5. SHRI SILVIUS CONDPAN: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) what is the present position in the
matter of construction of Bogibeel Rail-
cum-Road Bridge over river Brahmaputra
in Assam under Northern Frontier Railway,
which is a National Project;
(b) whether his Ministry would take-
up the double laning of railway tracks
within Assam upto Tinsukia under
Northern Frontier  Railway to facilitate the
railway users of the seven North-Eastern
States;
(c) whehter the Rangiya Zonal Head
Quarter has started functioning in its full
scale and if not, what are the reasons
therefor; and
(d) what is the present position of
conversion of Lumding-Badarpur route to
broad gauge?
Small caterers and vendors
*6. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Catering
Policy of 2005 has virtually removed small
catering and vending contractors whose
holding was confined to one stall and trolley
at A, B, and C stations;
(b) if so, what are the detailed reasons
therefor;
(c) whether it is also a fact that a number
of catering and vending stalls were allotted
to the big companies on all railway stations
after removing the small vending contractors
who were earning their livelihood through
these stalls; and
(d) if so, whether the above action is
not violating the constitutional right of small
contractors?
Subsidized fertilizers to small tea
growers
*7. SHRI BIRENDRA PRASAD
BAISHYA: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware about
the scarcity of fertilizers for small tea
growers in Assam;

3
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to mitigate this problem;
(c) whether it is a fact that small tea
growers have to buy fertilizers at higher prices
despite Government's claim that fertilizers
are supplied to farmers at subsidized rates;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps taken by Government to ensure
supply of subsidized fertilizers to small
tea growers; and
(e) whether Government would ensure
the allocation of sufficient quantity of
fertilizers to small tea growers?
Supply of fertilizers to Madhya
Pradesh
*8. SHRI RAGHUNANDAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) the supply made against the demand
of 6.25 lakh tonnes of Urea, 5 lakh tonnes
of D.A.P., 3 lakh tonnes of complex of N.P.,
0.70 lakh tonnes of M.O.P., 3.75 lakh
tonnes of Super Phosphate and 0.010 lakh
tonnes of other fertilizers for Kharif 2008
of Madhya Pradesh till date; and
(b) the shortfalls in the supply, if any,
and the reasons therefor?
Diseases due to untimely rains
*9. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that untimely
rains in many parts of the country from
May-June onward this year have given rise
to diseases like malaria, gastroenteritis, etc;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
check the diseases lest they assume
epidemic proportions?
Coverage of underdeveloped districts
under the National Dairy Plan
*10. SHRIMATI. MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY JAWAHARLAL
DARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether National Dairy Plan (NDP)
2007-08 to 2021-22 is covering only 323
developed districts rather than 283
underdeveloped districts where the need is
more urgent;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether these 283 underdeveloped
districts will be provided with requisite
infrastructure, technical know-how and
finance, so that they may also contribute
towards achievement of NDP target of 180
million tonnes of milk by 2021-22; and
(d) by when the backward and tribal
districts of Y avatmal would be covered
under NDP?
Loans provided by NAFED to private
companies
*11. SHRI K. CHANDRAN PILLAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Agricultural
Co-operative Marketing Federation of
Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

4
India Limited (NAFED) has provided loans
to private companies;
(b) if so, the total amount  NAFED has
given to private companies as loan, so
far;
(c) the details of companies which had
availed loan from NAFED, year-wise and
amount-wise;
(d) whether it is a fact that many private
companies are defaulters in repaying the
loan;
(e) if so, the details thereof; and
(f) the action taken to recover the
amount?
Polio eradication
*12. SHRI Y .P. TRIVEDI: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether polio patients are being
found in the country despite repetitive
rounds of vaccination under the Pulse Polio
Immunization Programme; and
(b) if so, the number thereof alongwith
State-wise details?
Fund allocation to Himachal Pradesh
under NRHM
*13. SHRIMATI VIPLOVE THAKUR:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) what is the total amount of money
allocated to Himachal Pradesh for the
financial year 2007-08 under the National
Rural Health Mission;
(b) what is the total amount of money
that has so far been utilized; and
(c) keeping in view the hilly and
difficult terrain in the State, what steps
have been taken to improve health
infrastructure in the State so that medical
facilities of the highest quality reach the
poorest of the poor?
Rationalising of fertilizer subsidy
*14. SHRI RAHUL BAJAJ: Will the
Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) what measures his Ministry is taking
to reduce and rationalize the fertilizer
subsidy; and
(b) what have been the negative effects
of the subsidy on rational use of fertilizers
in the country?
Shortage of edible oils
*15. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of shortage of edible
oils in the country and the quantum of edible
oils imported during the last Five years,
year-wise;
(b) the amount spent every year on the
import of edible oils;
(c) whether Government has fixed the
rate of imported edible oil at Rs. 45 per
litre;
Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

5
(d) whether Chhattisgarh Government
has fixed the rate of edible oil at Rs. 60 per
litre at their fair price shops; and
(e) whether in the States of Rajasthan,
Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu,
Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Uttarakhand,
Gujarat and Bihar, edible oil is being given
to fair price shop consumers at the rate
fixed by the Government of India?
Increase in the number of Kidney
patients
*16. SHRI THENNALA G.
BALAKRISHNA PILLAI: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
the number of kidney patients in the
country is increasing;
(b) if so, whether any study has been
conducted in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Green revolution
*17. SHRI PRABHAT JHA: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the first
green revolution in the present context is
not effective;
(b) if so, whether Government has taken
any steps to start second green revolution;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether it is also a fact that
Government has identified certain areas/
States for the second green revolution; and
(e) if so, the details thereof with the
funds allocated for the scheme?
Import of edible oil
*18. SHRI PRAKASH JA V ADEKAR:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided to import 1 million tonnes of
edible oil for distribution to the poor through
PDS with subsidy;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) since when the subsidized
distribution has started;
(d) the rate at which it is being
distributed; and
(e) how much subsidized edible oil has
been distributed till date?
Unmanned level crossings
*19. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the number of unmanned level
crossings currently in existence, Zone-wise
and the number of accidents occurred there
during the last three years;
(b) what are the measures taken to avert
such accidents and whether they are
adequate and effective; and
(c) whether there is any plan of action
with a time-frame to avoid the use of these
unmanned level crossings permanently by
going for alternative infrastructure like over
bridges/subways, etc.?

6
Wastage of agricultural food items
*20. SHRI M.V . MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as per Rabo
India Finance Ltd. wastage of agricultural
food items last year was to the extent of
Rs. 58,000 crores;
(b) if so, whether the wastage of
agricultural food items has been on the rise
over the last few years;
(c) the extent of such wastages in the
last five years, year-wise and State-wise;
(d) whether his Ministry is planning to
amend the Agricultural Produce Marketing
(Development & Regulation) Act to bring
down such wastages;
(e) if so, the details thereof;
(f) whether any emphasis has been laid
in the Eleventh Five Year Plan to address
this serious issue; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 11th October, 2008 Secretary-General.
Asvina 19, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Agriculture : 10, 11, 17, 20,

Distribution : 15, 18,
